explanation: A translation slides every point of a shape by the same fixed amount: dx to the right and dy up. Because every vertex moves by the identical translation vector, the image is congruent to the preimage with the same size, shape, and orientation, just relocated. The green arrow on one vertex shows that shared vector, and the yellow dashed outline animates the slide from the blue preimage to the pink image. Adjusting dx and dy moves the whole figure together; nothing stretches or rotates, which is what makes a translation a rigid motion.
bullets: Every point shifts by the same vector (dx, dy) — drawn in green.
Image (pink) is congruent to the preimage (blue): same size and shape.
Orientation is preserved; the shape does not flip or turn.
The yellow dashed shape animates the slide partway across.
